paper.title: Beacon: Detecting Broken Access Control Vulnerabilities in DBMSs via System Catalog Consistency Validation
paper.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages

summary.text: Beacon detects broken access control vulnerabilities in DBMSs by checking SQL operations against the system catalogs. Its premise is that catalog visibility should agree with a user's privileges: if an object is invisible to a user in the catalogs, that user should have no access to it, so any inconsistency indicates a privilege the user should not have. Applied to eight DBMSs it uncovered 39 previously unknown vulnerabilities, 19 giving privilege escalation and 20 unauthorised disclosure, all confirmed by vendors.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: A consistency oracle in the same spirit as SQLancer's, aimed at access control rather than query results. The abstract does not state that it builds on SQLancer.
supporting_excerpts: In this paper, we propose Beacon, which detects BAC vulnerabilities by validating the consistency between SQL operations and system catalogs.

Any inconsistency suggests that a user is exceeding their privileges, indicating a potential BAC vulnerability.We used Beacon to test eight popular DBMSs (e.g., MySQL and MariaDB), uncovering 39 previously unknown BAC vulnerabilities.

sources.note: Semantic Scholar records this paper as citing the publication that introduced Non-optimizing Reference Engine Construction (NoREC), Ternary Logic Partitioning (TLP), Cardinality Estimation Restriction Testing (CERT).
